sessions.feedback: A way to see whether a pre-market gap comes from earnings would help a lot, for example an earnings-date calendar or an 'earnings today' flag in the digest or scan. Without it I can't tell an earnings gap from an offering or a rumor. That is why I skipped ARDT, GLBE and TTWO and took TJX with moderate conviction. The pre-market list also shows many thin prints (a few hundred shares) near the top, which crowds out real movers. A minimum share count filter would help.

No news access made unusual pre-market movers (SLS +308%, AS +4.8%, TU last session) impossible to judge, so I skipped them. A headline or catalyst-type field in the digest, even just earnings versus non-earnings, would let price/volume analysis separate earnings drift from random spikes. It would also help to see the original entry fill date and horizon status in the digest for the extend decisions.
Nothing blocking. Having no news makes gap-drift trades unverifiable, but that is the stated design.

Session 2026-11-18.

Session 2026-11-18. SPY fell 1.0% on 11/17 (732.44, -2.3% over 5 days), with VIXY up. Pre-market SPY is +0.2% and QQQ +0.6%. CROX (158.79) and GKOS (243.25) are holding near highs with no pre-market trades. Both have stops (about 147 and 223) well below the price, and horizons run to about 12/2, so I held both. HD and LOW were down pre-market, so the move is TJX-specific. Stop is 4.5% below the fill, near the pre-gap close, with a +9% target and a 10-day horizon, probability 0.54. Skipped: ARDT (-20% pre-market after a +55% run, probably an offering or bad news, cause unknown, shortable), GLBE (-14% pre-market, probably earnings, short edge marginal after 0.25% slippage), TTWO (+5% after two down days, GTA VI launch 11/19, unknown cause), BRBR (+13%, $1.3B thin, 0.5% slippage), ZIM (+4%, unknown). Cash is about 77% after TJX. Next session: check TJX holds the gap (the 11/18 close should be above about 131). Check CROX 149.5 and GKOS 219 consolidation lows. ROST reports this week, so there is sympathy and event risk for TJX. Look for gap-on-heavy-volume setups after declines.
notes:
Notes (2026-11-18): Strategy is price/volume only, no news access. Open trades: GKOS (entry 228.57) and CROX (entry 145.06), both post-earnings-gap drift trades opened 10/29. Both were extended 11/17 to about 12/2 with stops of about 147 (CROX) and 223 (GKOS) and targets of about 182 and 282. On 11/17 SPY fell another 1.0% (732.44) and the 5-day move is -2.3%. CROX closed 158.79 (-0.8%) and GKOS 243.25 (-0.7%), so both still show relative strength, which is mild evidence for the drift thesis.

11/18: opened TJX long (7%) on an earnings-type gap of about +5% pre-market after 6 down days. HD and LOW were down pre-market, so the TJX move is idiosyncratic. Skipped ARDT (-20%, likely an offering after a +55% run, cause unknown), GLBE (-14% gap, post-earnings short with a marginal edge after 0.25% slippage) and TTWO (+5% after two down days, GTA VI launches 11/19, cause unknown).

Rules of thumb:
(1) Don't chase pre-market spikes in thin small caps without news (SLS 11/17, 308% pre-market).
(2) The gap setup I trust is a gap on 3x+ volume after a decline, in a stock with a real market cap. Slippage there is 0.1-0.25%.
(3) Shorting after a -15-20% gap with an unknown cause is a coin flip, so skip unless the pattern is clear.
(4) Cash was 84% before TJX. Deploy only on clear setups.

Open questions: does TJX hold the gap? Check the 11/18 close against about 131. If CROX or GKOS break below their consolidation lows (CROX 149.5, GKOS 219), close them. ROST reports this week, which is a sympathy and event risk for TJX.

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is a few high-quality trades.

- Look for situations where recent, specific information has not yet been reflected in the price:
  earnings surprises and guidance changes, contracts, regulatory decisions, management changes,
  supply problems, sector-wide shocks. Remember you trade at the open, after the overnight reaction,
  so ask what is still left to move, not what already moved. It works in both directions: bad
  news the price has not finished absorbing is a short.
- Prefer clear catalysts you can verify over vague narratives. A strong case beats a busy portfolio,
  so concentrate on your best ideas. Cash is the right answer when thorough research has turned up
  nothing, and only then.
- Size positions by conviction and by how much could go wrong. Set stops and targets you would
  actually stand behind.
- Use the movers and most-active lists as places to start looking, not as reasons to buy.

- You have no news access in this experiment: no headlines, no web search and no page reading.
  Your material is price and volume behaviour, so work through it properly: the movers and
  most-active lists, the sector moves in the digest, your open positions and the names in your
  notes. Pull history for the candidates, use search_symbols to find related companies in the same
  industry, and compare them. Your own notes are the only memory you have of anything you read.
